indicators.name: GDP Growth
indicators.label: Monthly GDP
indicators.what_it_means: Broadest measure of economic activity. GDP growth = more freight moving.

indicators.name: GDP YoY
indicators.label: GDP, year over year
indicators.what_it_means: GDP against the same month last year. The longer-term freight demand trend.

indicators.name: US GDP Growth
indicators.label: Quarterly GDP
indicators.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED
indicators.what_it_means: Broadest measure of US economic activity. GDP growth = more freight moving.

indicators.name: US GDP YoY
indicators.label: GDP, year over year
indicators.source: US Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED
indicators.what_it_means: GDP against the same quarter last year. The longer-term freight demand trend.

indicators.name: Fuel Cost
indicators.label: Fuel cost per 1,000 km
indicators.what_it_means: Per-1,000km fuel cost at current diesel prices. Used directly in rate quotes.

indicators.name: Fuel Spread
indicators.label: BC vs AB diesel spread
indicators.what_it_means: Wide gaps create arbitrage on cross-province lanes. BC diesel runs higher than AB.

indicators.name: US Fuel Cost
indicators.label: Fuel cost per 1,000 miles
indicators.what_it_means: Per-1,000-mile fuel cost at the US national average. Used directly in rate quotes.

indicators.name: US Fuel Spread
indicators.label: California vs Lower Atlantic diesel spread
indicators.what_it_means: The gap between the dearest and cheapest EIA district. Fuel where Lower Atlantic prices it.

indicators.name: CAD Impact
indicators.label: USD/CAD vs 30-day average
indicators.what_it_means: Weaker CAD = more competitive cross-border exports, higher input costs. Stronger CAD = cheaper US equipment/parts.

rates_snapshot.note: Rate data from DAT/Loadlink requires paid subscription. These are operating cost indicators that drive rate floors.

note: Public data from the US Bureau of Economic Analysis, EIA, Statistics Canada, NRCan and the Bank of Canada.
